title: Flood Insurance in Myrtle Beach: Zones, Maps and Your Loan
description: When your lender requires flood insurance in Myrtle Beach, how to read the flood zone map, local discounts by town, and the coverage you need.
h1: Flood Insurance in Myrtle Beach: When Your Mortgage Requires It
dek: Buying on the Grand Strand? Here's when your lender needs flood insurance, how to check the map, and the local discounts most buyers don't know about.

faq.q: Do I need flood insurance in Myrtle Beach?
faq.a: Only if the home is in a high-risk FEMA flood zone, one starting with A or V, or in a protected coastal barrier area. Then your lender requires it. In shaded or unshaded Zone X it's your choice, though homes there can still flood.

faq.q: Is flood insurance cheaper in Myrtle Beach?
faq.a: Federal flood policies in the City of Myrtle Beach get a 25% discount in high-risk zones and 10% elsewhere, through FEMA's Community Rating System. The City of North Myrtle Beach gets 20% and 10%, and the Town of Surfside Beach 15% and 5%.

faq.q: Is flood insurance required to be escrowed?
faq.a: Usually. Federally regulated lenders must collect flood premiums through escrow, with a few exceptions, so the premium is paid along with your monthly mortgage payment.

faq.q: Is there a waiting period for flood insurance when buying a house?
faq.a: No. A federal flood policy bought with a new loan takes effect at closing, as long as you apply and pay by then. Without a loan, a new policy normally starts 30 days after you apply and pay.

A flood certificate, or flood cert, is the lender's official record of a home's FEMA flood zone. The lender orders it after you apply. If the home is in a high-risk zone, flood insurance becomes a requirement of the loan.
